insight: For Tunisia, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have generally been a positive turning point, with the team gaining momentum in 4 out of 6 breaks, indicating a slight increase in performance after the pause. The numbers suggest that when Tunisia is not pressing before a hydration break, they tend to come out stronger, with an average increase in momentum of 0.120 minutes, which can be a significant advantage in a tight match. In contrast, when they are pressing before a break, their momentum actually decreases, as seen in the one instance where their average momentum dropped by 0.200 minutes, and they were unable to regain it after the pause. Overall, Tunisia seems to benefit from the brief respite, allowing them to regroup and refocus, which can be a crucial factor in their overall match strategy.
